paraphrase: E ma, the secret speech of the ḍākinīs: the non-dual nature is the abode of mahāmudrā; the Buddha, Dharma and Saṅgha are its nature; bowing to the bodhisattva, lord of bliss, I will explain.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (the Apabhraṃśa/Sanskrit original not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: sa dang chu dang me dang rlung dang nam mkha' rnams/ / lhan cig skyes pa'i ro gcig las ni gzhan yod min/ / srid dang mya ngan 'das pa gnyis su mi rtogs pa/ / 'di ni chos kyi dbyings kyi gnas lugs yin par bshad/ /

paraphrase: Earth, water, fire, wind and space are nothing other than the one taste of the innate; not conceiving saṃsāra and nirvāṇa as two is said to be the mode of the dharmadhātu.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (the Apabhraṃśa/Sanskrit original not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: kye ma rang la rang gis de nyid mtshon te ltos/ / ma yengs pa yi sems kyis lta dang bral gyur na/ / yengs pa'i sems kyis de nyid rtogs par mi 'gyur te/ / dngos po'i tshang tshing gseb tu de nyid nor bu stor/ /
original.edition: Derge Tengyur/Kangyur, Tōhoku D2264, digital edition by Esukhia and Barom Theksum Choling (github.com/Esukhia/derge-tengyur), file 052_རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ།_ཞི.txt — Tibetan translation, Wylie by the preparer

paraphrase: Kye ma, look and point out that reality by yourself in yourself; with an undistracted mind free of views (it is realized); a distracted mind does not realize it, and the jewel is lost in the thicket of things.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (the Apabhraṃśa/Sanskrit original not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: re dang dogs pa'i dug gis rnal 'byor sems myos na/ / lhan cig skyes pa'i ye shes gnas de 'ching bar 'gyur/ / kye ma rang bzhin bral ba'i de nyid bsgom du yod ma zer/ / gal te bsgom par bya dang sgom byed gnyis rtogs na/ / gnyis su 'dzin pa'i yid kyis byang chub sems spangs te/ / skyes bu de yis rang gis rang la sdig pa byas/ /

paraphrase: When the yogin's mind is intoxicated by the poison of hope and fear, the innate gnosis is bound; do not say the natural reality is something to be meditated; if one conceives meditation and meditator as two, the grasping mind abandons bodhicitta and one harms oneself.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (the Apabhraṃśa/Sanskrit original not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: kye ma bla ma'i zhal gyi bdud rtsi'i thigs pa ji snyed pa/ / des shes sngon 'gro pa yis rab tu blang bar bya/ / dus dang thabs la mkhas pas dus su ma bsten na/ / long bas rgyal po'i bang mdzod rku dang 'dra bar 'gyur/ / kye ma rin chen dbang dang bral ba'i skyes bu ni/ / gdol pa dman pa zhig gis rgyal por re smon bzhin/ / rig pa 'dzin pa'i rgyud rnams der bslus pas/ / mkha' 'gros chad pa bcad nas rdo rje'i dmyal bar ltung / /

paraphrase: Take the drops of nectar from the guru's mouth with the preliminaries; one skilled in time and means who does not rely on them at the right time is like a blind man stealing the king's treasury; a person without the precious consecration is like an outcaste hoping to be king; deceived by the vidyādhara tantras, he is punished by the ḍākinīs and falls into the vajra hell.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (the Apabhraṃśa/Sanskrit original not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: kye ma brtan pa'i sa la phyin nas dam tshig mi ldan na/ / rgyal pos chad pa gcod pa'i mi ni bzung ba ltar/ / rnam smin lcags kyus srog gi rlung ni bzung byas nas/ / khro chu khol ma khar blugs pa ni bzod par dka'/ /
original.edition: Derge Tengyur/Kangyur, Tōhoku D2264, digital edition by Esukhia and Barom Theksum Choling (github.com/Esukhia/derge-tengyur), file 052_རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ།_ཞི.txt — Tibetan translation, Wylie by the preparer

paraphrase: Kye ma, one who has reached the stable ground but lacks the pledges is like a man seized for the king's punishment; the karmic ripening, seizing his life-wind with an iron hook, pours boiling liquid into his mouth — hard to bear.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (the Apabhraṃśa/Sanskrit original not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: kye ma gnas lugs rtogs kyang dman pa'i spyod pa nyid byed na/ / rgyal po khri las bab nas phyag dar byed pa bzhin/ / zad mi shes pa'i bde ba chen po nyid spangs nas/ / 'khor ba'i bde ba dag la reg pa nyid kyis 'ching / /
original.edition: Derge Tengyur/Kangyur, Tōhoku D2264, digital edition by Esukhia and Barom Theksum Choling (github.com/Esukhia/derge-tengyur), file 052_རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ།_ཞི.txt — Tibetan translation, Wylie by the preparer

paraphrase: Kye ma, one who realizes the natural state but still acts basely is like a king who comes down from his throne to sweep the floor; abandoning inexhaustible great bliss he is bound by touching the pleasures of saṃsāra.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (the Apabhraṃśa/Sanskrit original not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: kye ma spros pa rnams dang bral ba'i rang gi sems mthong nas/ / spros pa rnams la ched du 'bad pa'i rnal 'byor ni/ / nor bu rin chen rnyed nas 'ching bu tshol ba bzhin/ / 'bad pa byas kyang snying po'i sa ni nam yang min/ /
original.edition: Derge Tengyur/Kangyur, Tōhoku D2264, digital edition by Esukhia and Barom Theksum Choling (github.com/Esukhia/derge-tengyur), file 052_རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ།_ཞི.txt — Tibetan translation, Wylie by the preparer

paraphrase: Kye ma, the yogin who, having seen his own mind free of elaboration, strives purposely at elaborations is like one who, having found a precious jewel, goes looking for a glass bead.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (the Apabhraṃśa/Sanskrit original not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: bla ma'i dus thabs bsten pa de ni cher rtogs la/ / shes rab pha rol phyin dang mdo gzhan las rnyed cing / / kun la sbyar ba'i sems ni rab tu bsgom par bya/ / phyi dang nang du blta ba med pa'i sems de ni/ /
original.edition: Derge Tengyur/Kangyur, Tōhoku D2264, digital edition by Esukhia and Barom Theksum Choling (github.com/Esukhia/derge-tengyur), file 052_རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ།_ཞི.txt — Tibetan translation, Wylie by the preparer

paraphrase: One should come to understand greatly by relying on the guru's time and means; it is found in the Prajñāpāramitā and other sūtras; meditate on the mind applied to everything, the mind that looks neither outside nor inside.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (the Apabhraṃśa/Sanskrit original not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: dkyil 'khor pa dang sbyin sreg pas stong zhing / / sngags dang phyag rgya rab gnas la sogs rnam bral ba/ / rgyud dang bstan bcos kun gyi bsgrub par mi nus pa'i/ / rdo rje ye shes 'di ni rang bzhin gnas na mdzes/ /

paraphrase: Empty of maṇḍala-makers and fire-offerers, free of mantra, mudrā, consecration of images and the like, this vajra gnosis, which no tantra or treatise can accomplish, is beautiful when it abides in its own nature.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (the Apabhraṃśa/Sanskrit original not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: bar snang mdzub mos mtshon pas bar snang mthong ba med/ / bla mas mtshon pa'i bla ma de yang de bzhin no/ /

paraphrase: Pointing to the sky with a finger does not show the sky; the guru pointed out by the guru is likewise.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (the Apabhraṃśa/Sanskrit original not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: mkhas pa thams cad snying la dug gis khyab par gyur/ / sems nyid rnal ma'i don ni kun gyis rtogs dka' ba/ / mtha' yis ma gos dri ma med pa'i snying po ni/ / rang bzhin gdod nas rnam pa kun gyi dpyad bya min/ / gal te dpyad na dug sbrul gtses pa kho nar zad/ / blo yis gzhag pa'i chos 'di thams cad rang gis stong / /
original.edition: Derge Tengyur/Kangyur, Tōhoku D2264, digital edition by Esukhia and Barom Theksum Choling (github.com/Esukhia/derge-tengyur), file 052_རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ།_ཞི.txt — Tibetan translation, Wylie by the preparer

paraphrase: The hearts of all scholars are pervaded by poison; the meaning of mind itself is hard for all to realize; the essence untouched by extremes is primordially not something to be analysed; if one analyses it one is merely bitten by the snake; all the dharmas posited by the intellect are empty of themselves.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (the Apabhraṃśa/Sanskrit original not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

paraphrase: The song describes the conduct (brtul zhugs spyod pa) of the realized yogin: entering towns, palaces, markets, feasts (gaṇacakra) and cremation grounds without fear, sleeping among ghosts, keeping company with outcastes, singing and dancing Heruka's dance, wearing bone ornaments and animal skins and carrying the khaṭvāṅga and bell, acting like a mad elephant; 'practising low dharmas, one is freed', says the arrow-maker.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (the Apabhraṃśa/Sanskrit original not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan
notes: Summary only. vv. 44–47 in this range describe the qualities of a consort (karmamudrā) and are not reproduced (restricted). The same song elsewhere (v. 19–20) warns against base conduct without realization.

paraphrase: The guru who shows all the various dharmas as one taste is to be received with devotion on the crown of one's head; the guru is the one who points out, the disciple's own heart the ground pointed to; he is the hero who destroys all suffering in an instant, the king of physicians, the supreme boat across the ocean of saṃsāra, the sun of gnosis — rely on him always.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (the Apabhraṃśa/Sanskrit original not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

paraphrase: E ma, the secret speech of the ḍākinīs: realizing the equality of means and wisdom, the innate is found from clear light; like the waxing moon it comes from habituation; the vajra master is the root of all attainments.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (the Apabhraṃśa/Sanskrit original not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

paraphrase: The dharmakāya, saṃbhogakāya and nirmāṇakāya, with the svābhāvikakāya, are to be known as cause and result; the svābhāvika body's bliss is the great enjoyment; through the power of aspiration and compassion the two form bodies arise, beautiful like the good vase, the wish-granting tree and the jewel, appearing variously to those to be trained — inconceivable emanations.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (the Apabhraṃśa/Sanskrit original not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.text: theg pa chen po bla med snying po'i lam 'di ni/ / 'bras bu lam du khyer nas gdod nas 'bras bur gnas/ / gzhan don phun sum tshogs pa 'bras bu'i mchog yin te/ / sbyangs pa gtso bor gyur pa sogs las de ni 'byung / /
original.edition: Derge Tengyur/Kangyur, Tōhoku D2264, digital edition by Esukhia and Barom Theksum Choling (github.com/Esukhia/derge-tengyur), file 052_རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ།_ཞི.txt — Tibetan translation, Wylie by the preparer

paraphrase: This path of the unsurpassed essence of the Great Vehicle takes the fruit as the path and abides as the fruit from the beginning; the perfect benefit of others is the supreme fruit.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (the Apabhraṃśa/Sanskrit original not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

original.edition: Derge Tengyur/Kangyur, Tōhoku D2264, digital edition by Esukhia and Barom Theksum Choling (github.com/Esukhia/derge-tengyur), file 052_རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ།_ཞི.txt — Tibetan translation, Wylie by the preparer

paraphrase: Liberation in an instant is called the dharmakāya; children say there is a ground of great bliss other than that liberation, but it is like a mirage; grounds, paths and buddhahood are all one, this very innate gnosis.
translation_basis: Tibetan translation (the Apabhraṃśa/Sanskrit original not consulted); paraphrase made by the unit from the Tibetan

paraphrase: Clearing away the chaff of speculation and elaboration, realizing this unsurpassed essence of meaning born of the natural faculties, one abides on the fourteenth ground; may beings, by the gradual and the simultaneous entry, attain mahāmudrā.
